authors: Fan F, Zhao C, Ren H, Lv L, Tian B, Wei G
title: External morphology and microstructure of the compound eye of fire ants, Solenopsis invicta Buren
why: The abstract (logged) gives eye type, ommatidia counts and rhabdom length for alates; the full text may give facet diameters or angles from which an interommatidial angle for the Sharpness row could be read. Its tables were not seen, so this is a chance, not a certainty.

title: Safe sites and the regeneration of Clethra alnifolia L. (Clethraceae) in wetland forests of central New Jersey
why: The only germination study of Clethra alnifolia found; its seedling safe-site work may show whether germination or establishment depends on light (the Woody Plant Seed Manual chapter cites only its stratification and light-dark incubation regime). Citation copied from the reference list of Griffin and Blazich, USDA seed manual chapter 'Clethra L.'.

authors: Montoyo YG, García M, Segovia Y
title: Light and electron microscopic studies on the retina of the booted eagle (Aquila pennata)
why: The abstract (logged for receptor classes) says the retina has areas of high cell density implying elevated acuity; the full text may give cone or ganglion cell densities from which a sampling angle and acuity for the booted eagle's Sharpness row could be computed, and may say whether a fovea is present.
